deities: Nagaraja (the serpent king - installed as Anantha/Vishnu swaroopa and Vasuki/Shiva spirit)
festivals: Mannarasala Ayilyam (Ayilyam star in the Malayalam month of Thulam, Oct-Nov; main festival)

history.dynasty: Legend: installed by Parasurama (mythological); hereditary priesthood of the Mannarasala Illam (Valiyamma)
history.period: Legendary antiquity; one travel source says 'about 1,000 years ago' - unverified; no authenticated founding inscription
history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the temple is at MANNARASALA village near Haripad (~3 km south-east of Haripad), not Alappuzha town (Alappuzha is the district). The largest and most famous serpent-worship temple in Kerala, set in a 16-acre dense forest grove (sarpa kavu) with 30,000-100,000 stone serpent images along paths and trees. Origin legend: Parasurama, creator of Kerala, installed Nagaraja - 'Brahma, Vishnu and Siva in one' - in the Thirthasthala surrounded by Mandara trees (Mandarasala) so that the poison of serpents would spread and make the land habitable; the installed deity represents Anantha (Vishnu aspect) and Vasuki (Shiva spirit). Uniquely, the chief priestess is a woman - the eldest female member of the Mannarasala Illam, revered as Mannarasala Amma / Valiyamma. Popular offerings include Uruli Kamazhthal (placing a bell-metal vessel upside down, sought by childless couples) and the curative turmeric-paste prasadam. Founding date is legend-based, not documented - marked unverified. Opening hours conflict across sources (see visitor info).

name: Mannarasala Sree Nagaraja Temple
town_description: Haripad is a temple town in Alappuzha district on the NH-66 coastal highway between Alappuzha and Kollam, sometimes called 'Kshethra Nagari' (town of temples). It is a railway and bus hub for the surrounding region. The Mannarasala Sree Nagaraja Temple lies about 3 km south-east of Haripad town in the forested village of Mannarasala.

travel.airport: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport - about 115 km; Cochin International about 105 km (verify).
travel.road: Near Haripad on NH-47/NH-66; cabs and auto-rickshaws from Haripad bus and railway stations (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October-November (Ayilyam festival); also July-February per one source (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): most sources list 5:00 am-12:00 pm and 5:30 pm-7:30 pm; one review-based source lists 7:00 am-11:00 am and 5:30 pm-7:00 pm; another lists 7:00 am-10:30 am and 6:00 pm-7:30 pm. Confirm before visiting.
